pr.title: Add explicit transaction handles and operation lifetime protection
pr.body:
Implements explicit synchronous transaction handles from litedb-org/LiteDB#3064 and #3067, including the native-admission stack from #132. Targets **`dev` at `5dd942a73`** and its safety framework from litedb-org/LiteDB#3034/#3045.

**Current candidate: `f95f0b0cd`**, a test-only successor to measured production source `19065cc1e`; their complete `LiteDB/` trees match. The latest [Shared reader review](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/pull/133#pullrequestreview-5365276527) and [facade callback follow-up](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/pull/133#issuecomment-5910144864) are addressed, including an additional close/reopen race found during independent validation. Fresh performance measurements are complete; **the full exact-head hosted CI/Safety gate remains pending**. The previous candidate's Windows x64/net8 failure was an unintended 100 ms normal-cleanup budget in the new callback test. This correction scopes that limit to the deliberate self-drain probe; production code and its deadline are unchanged. Original failed evidence is retained.

## Safety / regression evidence

- **Contracts and risk:** High-risk ownership/concurrency change affecting `durable-ack`, `recovery-generation`, `reader-snapshot`, `historical-input` and `query-meaning`. Preserve admission, formats, isolation and configured durability; intentionally add explicit handle outcomes and documented disposal/error contracts. [API and migration guide](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/f95f0b0cd/docs/transaction-handles.md).
- **Prior states and interactions:** Direct/Shared; ordinary, legacy and handle calls; concurrent handles and live cursors; pooled hosts; maintenance/close; encrypted/historical files; external writers; abandoned sessions; reused wrappers with fresh cores. Inherited recovery, compatibility and fuzz coverage remains required.
- **Failure outcomes:** Acknowledged commits survive the stated fault models; rolled-back writes stay absent; uncertain commits remain indeterminate. Close cancels blocked admission before draining work, and maintenance permits existing dependencies to finish. Cleanup preserves its own errors without repeating a peer's fatal error. External writes become visible after reacquisition and cold reopen. Shared parent final checkpointing remains explicitly best-effort; pin/child errors propagate after cleanup.
- **Evidence:** Sixteen registered comparisons: eight against actual `560529066`, three against actual `eb01f346e`, three against actual `e821ae747`, and two against published packages. Permanent guards, registered fault hooks, coverage dispositions and runtime/platform checks accompany them. The final production tree passes **658 relevant tests on each net8/net10**, zero failures/skips; the final allocation harness passes **13 cases on each runtime**. Independent combined late-reader/facade review passes **58 cases per runtime**. Counts overlap. All production library targets build; net462/net481 tests compile. All **96 CI-policy tests** pass. Current runs: [CI and Safety evidence](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/actions/runs/36714086574), [16 regression proofs](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/actions/runs/36714086262), [Fuzz](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/actions/runs/36714086265), [index compatibility](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/actions/runs/36714086292), [Shared production comparisons](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/actions/runs/36714086493). These must finish on this exact head, including actual CLR 4 and native platforms. [Finite gate and detailed dispositions](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/f95f0b0cd/docs/transaction-handles-safety-review.md); the immutable archive will be linked after hosted validation completes.
- **Coverage delta and residual concerns:** Replacements and CI/harness changes are recorded in the ledger; no new quarantine. Native partitions preserve the exact selection and reject missing/duplicate/empty results; discovery now matches VSTest case sensitivity. The pin-progress test deliberately replaces a combined startup/throughput budget with bounded startup and completed-write progress, a 60-second overall cap, held-pin negative controls and exact cold-state assertions. Its original Windows timeout remains **unknown in origin**, with no retrospective deadlock or runner-slowdown claim. The strongest counterexample is close/maintenance preventing a continuation it needs; forced interleavings, genuine-error controls and before/after proofs address it. Existing quarantines remain gaps. Evidence covers exceptions, process death and modeled persistence faults, not physical power removal. This is the affected PR's finite #3034 gate, not completion of the whole roadmap or repository protection/merge-queue configuration; post-merge validation is configured, not claimed executed.

## Behavior and review dispositions

`BeginTransaction()` creates an independent handle. Its collections, queries and readers stay bound across sequential thread handoff; ordinary calls remain independent. Overlapping use and callback reentry reject before execution, and completed/abandoned handles release session/application ownership.

The only integrated performance option is **Shared holder-worker and child `SharedEngine` wrapper reuse**. **Every transaction still releases native writer ownership and closes/reopens its storage core.** No coherent page cache survives an external writer. Plain/encrypted tests establish actual reuse, distinct core identity, external writer progress, refreshed indexed reads and cold reopen. Idle resources, coordination participation and mode-admission leases retire correctly; password/collation changes invalidate the wrapper. No group commit, batching, IPC service, retained native lock/core, atomic `SessionLifetime`, single-bound-scope or inline-close experiment is included.

CI corrections retain their failed evidence: three local-feed repros now route through the dedicated proof workflow; an existing callback test now expects the documented immediate close refusal while still checking the injected I/O error and native exclusion. The previous Linux ARM64/net10 allocation assertion observed 6,056 bytes; **its cause remains unknown**. The test now isolates measurement on a dedicated thread, retains the exact zero-byte requirement and 1,000 measured publications, verifies state publication, and includes an escaping-allocation control that fails the zero assertion at 24,000 bytes. The 19065 ARM64/net10 job passed both strict-zero and positive-control tests with runtime/architecture guards; the successor still requires its own full matrix. No measured retry/discard or threshold relaxation is used. The later Windows callback-test cleanup failure retains its exact log/TRX: the 100 ms probe was accidentally applied to normal teardown. The corrected test keeps that limit only for self-dependent callback cases and restores the prior deadline in `finally`; safe controls use the normal deadline. It passes 18 cases per runtime and still detects all six original failures on real `e821` per runtime, with six safe controls passing. Independent review found no weakened oracle.

The original eight enumerated production findings have fixes and permanent guards: Shared-close admission cancellation; maintenance fairness; raw-close waiter cancellation; nested Shared-owner begin rejection; disposed-child validation before abort handling; disposal racing session close; peer-fatal versus genuine cleanup errors; and stale-sort cleanup under writable ownership. Subsequent review found and fixed deferred-fatal, child capture/admission and scope-handoff variants. All original failures and mutation controls remain in the linked audit, including failed intermediate fixes and harness corrections.

The [follow-up review](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/pull/133#pullrequestreview-5364329616) and [additional findings](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/pull/133#issuecomment-5908951510) have these dispositions:

| Finding | Resolution and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Pin-close error skips Shared cleanup | Finish independent retirement, preserve primary/secondary errors, and preserve surviving-reader leases/snapshots. A real Linux OS I/O fault reproduces on `eb01` and passes the correction; a peer writer progresses before the surviving reader ends. |
| Shared parent final-checkpoint contract | Narrow documentation to its historical best-effort behavior; parent-only fault tests retain WAL and recover committed indexed data. Pin/child errors still propagate. |
| Raw-close callback dependency; ordinary callback self-wait | Reject fresh work behind close and same-handle callback lock self-waits; preserve unrelated operations and idle-handle handoff. Intermediate scope-release and refused-close/native-release defects have explicit guards; restore context before admission handoff and refuse raw callback disposal before mutating ownership. Raw disposal still cannot bound an arbitrary application callback that never returns. |
| Cancellable mutex polling | Windows uses blocking `WaitAny` with a scoped cancellation event/registration; Unix retains bounded waits because named-mutex `WaitAny` is unsupported there. Uncontended admission allocates neither. Cancellation, release and owner-death controls pass; source inspection alone establishes no performance attribution. |
| Cached `ReadTransform` | Bounded allegation refuted by original/current public probes and four new guards: constructor settings are snapshotted for ordinary calls and handles; the retained delegate's mutable target remains visible. |
| Hypothetical pre-persist Commit leak | Unconfirmed in supported public paths; four precondition/outcome/retry controls pass without changing Commit semantics. |
| Diagnostics and structural nits | Zero `ThreadID` is diagnostic. The unpruned per-path managed registry predates reuse and retains no native ownership/application graph. Scheduler duplication, unsupported drop/rename API shape and existing encoding are outside this correction. |

The newest review is addressed by checking all executing mutex-dependent cores before close changes state, preserving native protection when teardown is refused, and draining operations outside the Shared lock needed by callbacks. A closing-core fence prevents fresh opens from using a draining core. Forced owner-exit, pin, unleased-snapshot and fresh-open interleavings include plain/encrypted native exclusion, external writer progress and cold indexed/sentinel checks. Facade disposal from an owned ordinary-reader callback now refuses immediately; independent leased readers and non-owning facades retain their valid behavior. The guide also identifies the last ordinary reader's `Dispose()` as an idle pin-close error path. Actual before/fixed proofs retain the original failures, intermediate race and corrected plain/encrypted harness conditions.

Public compatibility: typed/BSON collections, Include/vector queries, indexes and `$cols`/`$indexes` metadata are bound; read-only handles cannot write. SQL, FileStorage and maintenance are not handle APIs; drop/rename and external/system query I/O reject. Unsupported custom/coordinated/decorated providers and Shared private storage/caller streams reject handles; Direct caller streams remain supported. Existing interface implementers gain no required members. Legacy signatures remain with CS0618 warnings and a documented warnings-as-errors migration. Known committed outcomes survive cleanup errors; disposed facade access throws `ObjectDisposedException`. Parameterless Shared begin remains unbounded; opt-in timeout/cancellation bounds begin admission separately from collection `TIMEOUT`.

## Production measurements

**Measured exact production source `19065cc1e`, identical library tree to test-only successor `f95f0b0cd`.** Production Release/net10, `TestingEnabled=false`, .NET 10.0.11 on Ubuntu 24.04.3 x64/ext4, tiering disabled, alternating fresh processes, four rounds per case, five seconds warmup plus five one-second windows. Every result/index/sentinel and cold-reopen check passed; no measured windows were discarded. No local builds/tests/profiles or artifact collection/compression overlapped timing; text editing and metadata inspection continued. Other host load was uncontrolled. Rates are medians of process rates; gains are medians of paired rates, so they need not equal the displayed rate quotient. Allocation is process-wide, including holder-worker activity.

| Reads per Shared handle | Pre-reuse `c8c0cfab6` tx/s | Final tx/s | Paired gain | Before bytes/tx | Final bytes/tx |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 1,449.7 | 1,869.8 | 1.292× | 227,784 | 220,946 |
| 1 | 1,302.2 | 1,703.9 | 1.308× | 237,908 | 231,078 |
| 10 | 1,130.4 | 1,417.7 | 1.245× | 302,141 | 295,381 |

One-read handles improve **30.8% paired throughput**, with **2.9% less managed allocation**. **The experimental 4.69× / ~155 KB result was not reproduced.** These read-only transactions measure lifecycle cost, not durable-write throughput. The results include required core/admission/coordination cleanup and intervening correctness fixes: final implementation versus pre-reuse head, not an isolated attribution of every cost to wrapper reuse.

Matching comparisons against current upstream `dev` and the stacked parent:

| Workload | dev `5dd942a73` ops/s | Parent `49c327cf1` ops/s | Final ops/s | Paired vs dev | Paired vs parent |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Direct ordinary read | 96,289.9 | 88,262.1 | 81,832.3 | -15.2% | -6.4% |
| Direct legacy begin/read/commit | 93,657.4 | 86,631.9 | 74,092.7 | -21.0% | -15.1% |
| Direct attach/count/dispose | 7,088.2 | 16,680.8 | 10,977.2 | +55.8% | -33.4% |
| Shared ordinary read | 50,277.3 | 50,985.4 | 46,101.2 | -8.0% | -8.9% |
| Shared legacy begin/read/commit | 8,340.6 | 7,900.2 | 7,630.2 | -8.5% | -3.4% |

Read regressions remain explicit. Ordinary Direct allocation is 10,112 / 10,264 / 10,248 bytes per operation (dev/parent/final), so allocation volume alone does not explain the cost. The attach results are consistent with #132's pooled host benefit and #133's added lifetime/close machinery, but this campaign does not isolate those component costs. Earlier profiling and isolated guard/thread experiments remain in the historical report below; no broader counter, context or inline-close optimization is included. Performance acceptance is separate from safety qualification.

All **84 comparison processes and 420 measured windows** are retained and verified, including exact runner/library binaries, configurations, process ordering and paired ratios. The immutable archive will be linked with the final CI evidence.

<details>
<summary>Historical options and proof branches (not current-candidate measurements)</summary>


### Historical independent performance options — separate proof branches

**Only the Shared holder + child-wrapper option is now integrated, with fresh measurements above. All other experiments remain separate and are not included. The numbers in this historical options section describe the original proof branches.** [Full report](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/t3code/benchmark-group-commit-experiments/docs/transaction-performance-options.md), [controller source and replay instructions](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/tree/t3code/benchmark-group-commit-experiments/tools/WriteControllerExperiments), and [raw results, traces, exact measured binaries and test evidence](https://github.com/litedb-org/LiteDB-Artifacts/tree/2d58276b767d82d01d894b3af6bceb5048f47bd1/pull-requests/JKamsker-LiteDB-133/2026-09-30-options). All comparisons use production Release/net10.0 with `TestingEnabled=false`, tiering disabled, the same Ubuntu/ext4 host, and alternating fresh-process order. Host load is uncontrolled; these are local descriptive results. No measured samples were discarded.

**Ownership experiments, each compared independently with the PR head:**

| Option | Measured effect | Assessment / proof branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reuse Shared holder threads | +25.5% one-read handle throughput; 1,302→1,634 tx/s | [Thread-only proof](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/tree/experiment/pr133-shared-worker) |
| Reuse holder + child SharedEngine wrapper | **4.69× one-read throughput**, 1,302→6,064 tx/s; allocation 238→155 KB/tx. Zero reads 6.04×; ten reads 3.51× | [Original child proof; correctness fixes required](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/tree/experiment/pr133-shared-child) |
| Atomic SessionLifetime admission | Direct ordinary +1.3%, Direct legacy +2.3%, Shared ordinary −1.4% | [Small/mixed result](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/tree/experiment/pr133-session-refcount) |
| One bound context scope | Direct handles +1.7%, Shared handles +0.9% | [Small improvement](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/tree/experiment/pr133-single-scope) |
| Inline idle close | Attach/count/dispose +41.3% | **[Rejected upper bound](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/tree/experiment/pr133-inline-close): fails the existing bounded-close regression.** Idle final release can still block. |

**The original child proof retained its Shared mode-admission lease and could retain mapped coordination participation. It also missed changed password/collation settings. The current integration fixes those differences; the current measurements above include those cleanup costs.**

The Shared proofs release native writer ownership between transactions. The child-wrapper cache is per originating session, and **the storage core still closes/reopens** so external writes are observed. Plain/encrypted interprocess tests verify writer progress, reuse, refreshed records and cold reopen. Retaining a coherent storage core across external writes remains a separate protocol change. Independent traces recorded 6,216 versus 9 thread-creation events for the head versus each reuse variant over about six seconds; these are event counts, not live threads or throughput. Most measured gain came from keeping the child wrapper beyond thread reuse alone.

Inspection also corrected the nested-guard hypothesis: Dispatch's `Session.Enter()` is an EngineContext thread-static scope, not another SessionLifetime monitor. The tested scope variant removes the redundant ordinary adapter only for internal TransactionEngine calls, preserving callback isolation and one-use dispatch authorization. Broad allocation pooling was not needed for the observed Shared allocation reduction.

**Durable-write baseline against dev:** one caller measured Direct 186.0→187.6 writes/s (+0.8% paired) and Shared 117.4→118.3 (+1.0%). Sixteen callers measured Direct −2.8% and Shared −1.1% paired. This small-insert workload does not show the large regression seen in reads. It differs from the older write table's updates to existing rows; compare within each matrix.

**Queued writes / separate-process IPC, PR-head library, sixteen callers:**

| Strategy | Writes/s | Median process p99 | Paired throughput vs Direct |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Direct ordinary | 164.0 | 394.3 ms | 1.00× |
| Shared ordinary | 113.9 | 168.0 ms | 0.69× |
| Existing CoordinatedEngine | 154.1 | 485.9 ms | 0.94× |
| Dedicated queue, one commit/request | 184.0 | 118.3 ms | 1.12× |
| Queue, batch cap 32, no linger | 2,008.1 | 40.5 ms | 12.22× |
| Queue, batch cap 32, 1ms linger | 2,152.9 | 39.4 ms | 13.16× |
| IPC queue, one commit/request | 182.7 | 120.7 ms | 1.11× |
| IPC queue, batch cap 32, 1ms linger | **2,078.4** | **37.2 ms** | **12.64×** |

Four fresh processes per strategy/caller count, three seconds warmup and five seconds measurement; every ID, payload, indexed result and unrelated sentinel is checked on two cold reopens. Single-caller Direct measured 187.0 writes/s; the zero-linger queue 186.7, the 1ms batching queue 154.6 and IPC batching 150.4. **Linger costs roughly 18–20% at low load.** Sampled peak WAL at sixteen callers is ~13.4 MiB Direct, ~13.1 MiB existing coordinator, ~8 MiB queued/IPC and <0.5 MiB Shared; checkpoint/close schedules and in-flight transactions differ. Full ranges, client/server CPU, allocation and drain measurements are in the report. IPC client allocation excludes the server.

**Semantics and limits:** this prototype coalesces immutable insert commands into **one atomic transaction per batch**, with one confirmed-WAL sync before acknowledgements. It does not group already-open independent transactions or separate WAL confirmations. One invalid duplicate rolls back its whole batch. Commit/I/O failure stops the writer; lost IPC replies remain indeterminate, with no automatic retry or durable inbox. Same-collection engine-level group commit requires a separate lock/publication/recovery design. The IPC proof owns exclusive Direct admission for its lifetime and only exposes writes; other processes cannot open ordinary Direct/Shared readers alongside it. A usable service needs a read/snapshot API or integration with the existing coordinator.

**Safety evidence:** 17 controller scenarios pass, including no early acknowledgement, exact commit-sync counting, batch rollback, queue saturation/drain, partial I/O and failed/post-sync errors, encrypted durable-image recovery, real process kills, truncated IPC frames and a durable write with a lost reply. The current library also passes 102 relevant storage/failure/process regressions. Viable library variants pass their relevant net8.0/net10.0 suites (116–149 tests per partition; child reuse also passes 82 Shared tests); all production library targets build. The naive inline-close failure is why that option is rejected. These are local Linux proofs, not Windows/macOS validation or hosted-CI claims for the alternative branches.

The archive retains all **240 measured processes**: 60 upstream comparisons, 84 ownership comparisons and 96 durable-write runs. These historical results motivated holder/wrapper reuse. The current implementation and fresh measurements are above; the other options remain separate.

</details>

baseCommit.message:
Make safety evidence and coverage accounting checkable in CI (#3034) (#3045)

Make the PR safety review and integrated regression audits of #3034 checkable:

- Safety section: every PR answers the five evidence prompts and names each
  contract its changed paths implicate (contracts.json, check_pr_section.py).
- Coverage accounting: removed tests, skips, weaker assertions, fixture, corpus,
  fuzz, fault-evidence and CI-config changes need a disposition added by the same
  change (coverage-ledger.json, check_coverage_regression.py).
- Fault-point registry: all 66 named hooks plus every DEBUG/TESTING delegate,
  with evidence that names its hook (fault-points.json, check_fault_points.py).
- Safety evidence job: required jobs, legs, revision, discovery completeness and
  never-executed tests are checked from the uploaded results.
- Regression proofs: a fix proves its repro against a real known-bad state
  (published package, dev commit or PR commit); known bad must fail and the PR
  head must pass. PRs labelled bug or bugfix-fix must add one. An informational
  Evidence check and advisory labels show tests added and proofs proven.
- Published-prerelease compatibility job, merge_group triggers, docs.
- Gaps closed: startup tail-trim and reclaim-lock hooks tested,
  SimulateDataWriteFail wired and tested, five never-run tests running again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
